model.description: 'random' (the default): the random-effects model, whose test allows for the studies' true effects differing; 'fixed': the fixed-effect model, which assumes they don't.

template_two_level.description: People nested in groups (for example pupils in classes, or employees in teams), with a predictor measured on each person (X, centred within its group) and one measured on each group (W): the linear mixed model y ~ X + W + X:W + (1 + X | group). Tests X's effect within groups, W's effect between groups, or the cross-level interaction (whether X's effect depends on W). Simulated with simr's powerSim() on a model built by makeLmer(), testing the effect with lmerTest's Satterthwaite t test (simr's method 'sa'), as E33 does. X takes the same evenly spread standard normal values in every group (normal quantiles, so X is centred within groups and has SD 1); W takes evenly spread standard normal values across the groups. goal > n is the total number of people, a whole number of groups of population > cluster_size. A yes/no outcome (Y binary, population > metric 'probability') is a logistic mixed model built by makeGlmer(): the chance of 'yes' for a typical group at the average X and W (population > probability), every effect and SD on the log-odds scale and no residual SD, tested by glmer's Wald z test (method 'wald') or the likelihood-ratio test ('likelihood_ratio'). Three levels (population > groups_per_site given): the groups are in sites (e.g. classes in schools), with Z measured on each site, in y ~ x + w + z + x:w + x:z + (1 + x | site) + (1 + x | site:group) (the site X slope only when sd_site_slope is above 0); W is spread across each site's groups and Z across the sites, so the three are uncorrelated; goal > n is then a whole number of sites of cluster_size x groups_per_site people. Tests also Z's effect between sites ('site_effect') or X's interaction with Z ('site_interaction').

metric.description: 'raw' for a score outcome (in its own units); 'probability' for a yes/no outcome (the effects and SDs on the log-odds scale).

probability.description: Yes/no outcome only: the chance of 'yes' for a typical group at the average X and W.

b_X.description: X's effect within groups: the change in the outcome, in its own units, for one SD more of X than the group's average.

b_W.description: W's effect between groups: the change in a group's average outcome for one SD more of W.

b_XW.description: The cross-level interaction: how much X's effect changes for one SD more of W.

b_Z.description: Three levels only: Z's effect between sites, the change in a site's average outcome for one SD more of Z.

b_XZ.description: Three levels only: X's interaction with Z, how much X's effect changes for one SD more of Z.

sd_group.description: SD of the groups' random intercepts: how much groups' average outcomes differ beyond W.

sd_group_slope.description: SD of the groups' random X slopes: how much X's effect differs between groups beyond W.

r_group.description: Correlation between the groups' intercepts and X slopes. 0 if omitted.

sd_site.description: Three levels only: SD of the sites' random intercepts beyond Z.

sd_site_slope.description: Three levels only: SD of the sites' random X slopes beyond Z. 0 if omitted.

sd_residual.description: Score outcome only: SD of the residual, how much people differ within a group.

cluster_size.description: People in each group (the same in every group).

groups_per_site.description: Three levels only: groups in each site (the same in every site). Giving it makes the design three levels.

template_crossed_conditions.description: Participants respond to many items (stimuli) in three or more conditions, every participant in every condition (or, when X is a between factor, each participant in one condition: the participants split equally, a participant intercept only, every participant responding to every item or to their condition's block of items): a linear mixed model y ~ cond + (1 | participant) + (1 | participant:cond) + (1 | item), with cond a factor in treatment coding (each coefficient a condition's mean minus the first condition's), one participant-by-condition variance shared by every condition, and, with every item in every condition (item_design 'within'), an optional item-by-condition variance, (1 | item:cond). Simulated with simr's powerSim() on a model built by makeLmer(), testing that the conditions differ with lmerTest's Satterthwaite F test (effect 'condition'), or one pair of conditions with the Satterthwaite t test adjusted for all the pairs by stats::p.adjust() (effect 'pairwise'). goal > n is the number of participants; every participant responds to every item. With a yes/no outcome (Y binary, population > metric 'probability'), a logistic mixed model fitted by glmer: the probabilities per condition for a typical participant and item, every SD on the log-odds scale, no residual SD, and the test target_test > method 'wald' (glmer's Wald z test; for three or more conditions simr's Wald chi-square test; for a pair car's Wald test of its contrast) or 'likelihood_ratio' (the model against one without the conditions' differences, or for a pair without that pair's difference).

metric.description: 'raw' for a score outcome (means or a difference in the outcome's units); 'probability' for a yes/no outcome (Y binary), whose probabilities are those of a typical participant and item and whose SDs are on the log-odds scale.

probabilities.description: Yes/no outcome only: the chance of 'yes' in each condition (one per condition, in the order of X's levels) for a typical participant and item, that is with every random effect 0.

means.description: Each condition's mean, in the order of X's levels, in the outcome's units.

sd_participant.description: SD of the participants' random intercepts: how much participants' average responses differ.

sd_participant_condition.description: Conditions within participants (X a within factor; required): sD of the participant-by-condition effects: how much each participant's responses in a condition differ from what their average and the condition's mean predict, the same for every condition (random intercepts for participant:cond). Not used when X is a between factor.

sd_item.description: SD of the items' random intercepts: how much items' average responses differ.

sd_item_condition.description: Every item in every condition only (item_design 'within'): SD of the item-by-condition effects (random intercepts for item:cond). 0 if omitted.

sd_residual.description: SD of the residual: trial-to-trial variation within a participant and item.

items.description: Total number of items. With items between conditions, they are split equally, one block per condition, so the number must be a multiple of the number of conditions.

item_design.description: 'between' (the default): each item appears in one condition only. 'within': every item appears in every condition.

template_meta_subgroups.description: A planned meta-analysis that tests whether the average effect differs between kinds of studies (a categorical moderator, subgroup analysis): the k studies split equally between the kinds, each kind with its own average effect, every study of the same size. The test is the between-groups Q test: under the fixed-effect model metapower's mod_power(); under the random-effects model the Hartung-Knapp test by default (metafor's rma() with the kinds as a moderator, test = 'knha', simulated with Spower), or metapower's test (target_test > test "z"). goal > n is the number of studies.

metric.description: The effect size each study gives: 'd', a standardised mean difference between two groups, or 'r', a correlation.

study_size.description: The number of participants in a typical study, both groups together for d (metapower splits them equally).

i2.description: Heterogeneity as I-squared: the share of the variation between the studies' effects that isn't sampling error (0 for none). Used by the random-effects model; Valentine, Pigott and Rothstein (2010), following Higgins and colleagues, describe 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 as small, moderate and large degrees of heterogeneity.

effects.description: Each kind of study's average effect (Cohen's d, or r between -1 and 1), e.g. lab then online; the studies are split equally between the kinds.

model.description: 'random' (the default): the random-effects model, whose test allows for the studies' true effects differing; 'fixed': the fixed-effect model, which assumes they don't.

template_precision_two_groups.description: The confidence interval for Cohen's d between two equal groups (MBESS's ss.aipe.smd(), with the interval from the noncentral t, MBESS's ci.smd()). n is the total; each group has half.

d.description: Cohen's d expected in the population (the interval's width depends on it a little).

template_precision_one_group.description: The confidence interval for a standardised mean (the mean's distance from a fixed value, in SDs), one group (MBESS's ss.aipe.sm(), with the interval from the noncentral t, MBESS's ci.sm()).

d.description: The standardised mean expected: (mean - fixed value) / SD.

template_precision_paired.description: The confidence interval for d_z, the mean difference between two paired measurements divided by the SD of the differences (MBESS's ss.aipe.sm() on the differences). n is the number of pairs.

template_precision_correlation.description: The confidence interval for a correlation (presize's prec_cor(): Fisher's z for Pearson's r, with the variance corrections presize uses for Spearman's and Kendall's).

r.description: The correlation expected in the population.

template_precision_proportion.description: The confidence interval for one proportion (presize's prec_prop()): Wilson's interval by default, or Agresti-Coull, the exact (Clopper-Pearson) or the Wald interval.

p.description: The proportion expected in the population.

n.description: For dyadic data: the number of dyads (pairs), not people.

template_apim.description: The actor-partner interdependence model (APIM) for pairs of people (dyads): each member's X predicts their own Y (the actor effect) and their partner's Y (the partner effect), with the two members' X correlated and their Y residuals correlated. Paths are standardised. With distinguishable members (population > distinguishable true, e.g. woman and man) each member has their own actor and partner effect; with indistinguishable members (e.g. same-sex friends) one actor and one partner effect are shared, and the model is fitted with them constrained equal. Simulated with power4mome (data from the population model, the APIM fitted by lavaan), the chosen effect tested by its Wald z test. goal > n is the number of dyads.

distinguishable.description: true when the members can be told apart in a way that matters (woman and man, parent and child); false when they can't (same-sex friends, twins).

members.description: Distinguishable members only: their names, first member first. 'Member 1' and 'Member 2' if omitted.

actor.description: Indistinguishable members: the standardised actor effect (a person's X on their own Y).

partner.description: Indistinguishable members: the standardised partner effect (a person's X on their partner's Y).

actor_1.description: Distinguishable members: member 1's X on member 1's Y.

actor_2.description: Distinguishable members: member 2's X on member 2's Y.

partner_12.description: Distinguishable members: member 1's X on member 2's Y.

partner_21.description: Distinguishable members: member 2's X on member 1's Y.

r_x.description: The correlation of the two members' X.

r_y.description: The correlation of the two members' Y beyond what their X explain (the residual correlation, often called non-independence).

effect.description: The effect tested, or several tested together (joint power: every one significant in the same study): indistinguishable members 'actor', 'partner' or 'actor_and_partner'; distinguishable members 'actor_1', 'actor_2', 'partner_12', 'partner_21', 'both_actors', 'both_partners' or 'all_four'.

template_three_level.description: Three levels: people (level 1) in groups (level 2, e.g. classes) in sites (level 3, e.g. schools), with two conditions assigned to whole sites, to groups within each site, or to people within each group (population > assignment). On the scale of the outcome's total SD: the effect d, the sites' and groups' shares of the variance (icc_site, icc_group), and when the condition is assigned below the sites, the share of variance in its effect across sites (icc_effect_site) and, when assigned to people, across groups (icc_effect_group): y ~ cond + (1 + cond | site) + (1 + cond | site:group), with cond coded -0.5 and 0.5 and the condition's terms only where they apply. Simulated with simr's powerSim() on a model built by makeLmer(), testing the condition with lmerTest's Satterthwaite t test. goal > n is the number of people, a whole number of sites (an even number when whole sites are assigned). A yes/no outcome (Y binary, population > metric 'probability') is a logistic mixed model built by makeGlmer(): each condition's chance of 'yes' for a typical site and group (population > probabilities), and in place of the shares of variance the SDs of the sites' and groups' intercepts and of the effect across sites or groups, on the log-odds scale (sd_site, sd_group, sd_effect_site, sd_effect_group); tested by glmer's Wald z test (method 'wald') or the likelihood-ratio test ('likelihood_ratio').

metric.description: 'standardised' for a score outcome (on the scale of its total SD); 'probability' for a yes/no outcome (the SDs on the log-odds scale).

d.description: Score outcome only: the difference between conditions (second minus first) over the outcome's total SD.

icc_site.description: Score outcome only: the share of the outcome's total variance between sites (e.g. schools).

icc_group.description: Score outcome only: the share of the outcome's total variance between groups within sites (e.g. classes within schools).

icc_effect_site.description: Score outcome only: conditions assigned below the sites only: the share of the total variance in the effect across sites. 0 if omitted.

icc_effect_group.description: Score outcome only: conditions assigned to people only: the share of the total variance in the effect across groups. 0 if omitted.

probabilities.description: Yes/no outcome only: the chance of 'yes' in each condition (first, then second) for a typical site and group.

sd_site.description: Yes/no outcome only: SD of the sites' intercepts, on the log-odds scale.

sd_group.description: Yes/no outcome only: SD of the groups' intercepts within sites, on the log-odds scale.

sd_effect_site.description: Yes/no outcome only: Conditions assigned below the sites only: SD of the effect across sites. 0 if omitted, on the log-odds scale.

sd_effect_group.description: Yes/no outcome only: Conditions assigned to people only: SD of the effect across groups. 0 if omitted, on the log-odds scale.

assignment.description: What is assigned to the conditions: 'site' (whole sites), 'group' (groups within each site, half of each site's groups in each condition) or 'person' (people within each group, half of each group in each).

template_item_predictor.description: Participants respond to many items that differ on a score X measured on each item (e.g. word frequency), standardised across the items: a linear mixed model y ~ x + (1 + x | participant) + (1 | item), the effect of X per SD of X, each participant with their own slope on X, and the items varying beyond what X explains. Simulated with simr's powerSim() on a model built by makeLmer() (or makeGlmer() for a yes/no outcome), testing X with lmerTest's Satterthwaite t test, or for a yes/no outcome glmer's Wald z test or the likelihood-ratio test. goal > n is the number of participants; every participant responds to every item. With population > x_level 'trial' (1 November 2026) X is measured on each trial instead (e.g. a stimulus duration that varies from trial to trial): each participant meets every value once, rotated across the items, so X varies within items too, and its effect may vary across items (sd_item_slope): y ~ x + (1 + x | participant) + (1 + x | item).

metric.description: 'raw' for a score outcome (in its own units); 'probability' for a yes/no outcome (the SDs and the slope on the log-odds scale).

x_level.description: Where X is measured: 'item' (the default; one value per item) or 'trial' (each participant's values rotated across the items, so X varies within items).

slope.description: The effect of one SD more of X: in the outcome's units, or on the log odds for a yes/no outcome.

probability.description: Yes/no outcome only: the chance of 'yes' at the items' average X, for a typical participant and item.

sd_participant_slope.description: SD of the participants' slopes on X: how much X's effect differs between participants.

r_participant.description: Correlation of participants' intercepts and slopes. 0 if omitted.

sd_item.description: SD of the items' intercepts beyond what X explains.

sd_item_slope.description: X measured on each trial only: SD of the items' slopes on X. 0 if omitted.

sd_residual.description: Score outcome only: the residual SD.

template_precision_mean_difference.description: The confidence interval for the difference between two groups' means in the outcome's own units (presize's prec_meandiff(), two equal groups, equal variances). goal > n is the total of both groups.

difference.description: The expected difference between the means (second group minus first), in the outcome's units.

sd.description: The outcome's SD within each group (the same in both).

template_precision_odds_ratio.description: The confidence interval for the odds ratio between two groups (presize's prec_or()): the independence-smoothed logit interval by default (presize's own default), or Gart's or Woolf's. goal > n is the total of both groups; goal > width is the width on the odds-ratio scale.

p1.description: The expected proportion of 'yes' in the first group.

p2.description: The expected proportion of 'yes' in the second group.

template_precision_icc.description: The confidence interval for an intraclass correlation (presize's prec_icc()): k ratings of each subject. goal > n is the number of subjects.

raters.description: The number of ratings (raters or occasions) of each subject.

template_precision_regression_coefficien.description: The confidence interval for one standardised regression coefficient in a multiple regression (MBESS's ss.aipe.reg.coef(), with assurance if asked); at a given n, the width is the narrowest for which ss.aipe.reg.coef() needs no more than n, and the interval is symmetric about b. goal > n is the number of participants.

b.description: The expected standardised coefficient of X.

r2.description: R-squared of the full model (all predictors).

r2_predictor.description: R-squared of X on the other predictors (0 if X is the only predictor or uncorrelated with them).

predictors.description: The number of predictors in the model, X included.
